import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and visually appealing theme
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a multi-dimensional scatter plot (bubble chart)
# This allows us to visualize relationships between price, megapixels, ISO, sensor, and body type.
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='max_iso',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Control the min and max size of the bubbles
    alpha=0.8,
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5
)

# Add annotations for each point to identify the camera
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    plt.text(
        x=df['price_usd'][i],
        y=df['megapixels'][i] + 0.8, # Offset text slightly above the point
        s=f"{df['brand'][i]} ({df['model_year'][i]})",
        fontdict=dict(color='black', size=11, weight='semibold'),
        ha='center'
    )

# --- Formatting and Styling ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Market Analysis: Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', pad=25)
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the x-axis to display currency
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=0, fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Enhance the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually set legend titles for clarity
legend_titles = ['Sensor Type', 'Body Type', 'Max ISO']
# Group the legend items
sensor_type_legend = plt.legend(handles[1:6], labels[1:6], title=legend_titles[0], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', title_fontsize=13, fontsize=11)
ax.add_artist(sensor_type_legend)
body_type_legend = plt.legend(handles[6:10], labels[6:10], title=legend_titles[1], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.65), loc='upper left', title_fontsize=13, fontsize=11)
ax.add_artist(body_type_legend)
max_iso_legend = plt.legend(handles[10:], labels[10:], title=legend_titles[2], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.35), loc='upper left', title_fontsize=13, fontsize=11)

# Set plot limits to provide better spacing
ax.set_xlim(0, df['price_usd'].max() + 500)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['megapixels'].max() + 10)

# Use tight_layout to ensure all elements fit
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legends

# Save the final visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
